column3: “God of my rock” is rendered “My God, my rock,” and “place of escape” as “refuge”; NASB adds “my stronghold.”
“The one to be praised” is rendered “who is worthy to be praised.”
“Breakers of death” is rendered “waves of death,” and “torrents of worthlessness” as “torrents of destruction.”
“It burned to Him” is rendered “He was angry.”
“Nose” is rendered “nostrils,” and “from Him” as “by it.”
Close to the Hebrew; many manuscripts read “He soared” instead of “He appeared.”
“A sieve of waters” (Hebrew חַשְׁרַת־) is rendered “a mass of waters”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB uses past tense (“were … did not depart”).
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “Therefore.”
“Faithful” is rendered “kind,” and “a blameless mighty man” as “the blameless.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “whom.”
“I run a marauding band” is rendered “I can run upon a troop.”
